h1: The 7 Best Power Strips with USB Ports for Desks and Living Rooms, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Power Strips with USB Ports: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 7 power strips with USB ports, compared on joule rating, outlet spacing, USB-C, cord length and safety certification.
mainKeyword: best power strips with usb ports
summary: The 12-outlet strip with six USB ports and 2400 joules is the best all-rounder, with three USB-C ports and wide spacing. ALESTOR is the pick for surge protection at 2700 joules, Nuetsa is the best flat-plug option, and Mifaso reaches furthest with a 10 ft cord.
intro: Most power strips with USB ports are really phone chargers with a surge protector bolted on, and the USB spec is usually the weaker half. Two numbers decide whether a strip is worth owning: the joule rating that protects your gear and the amperage that charges it. A strip that lists neither is an extension cord with lights on it.

We ranked seven strips, all under $30, by surge rating, certification, outlet spacing, USB-C and cord length. Where a listing names no joule figure or safety mark, we say so, because a strip that cannot prove its protection is not protecting anything. The best pick is not the one with the highest joule number.

products.name: 12-Outlet Surge Protector with 6 USB Ports (3 USB-C), 2400J
products.verdict: Twelve wide-spaced outlets, three USB-C ports and 2400 joules in one 6 ft strip.
products.description:
This strip turns one wall outlet into 12 AC outlets and adds six USB ports, three USB-A and three USB-C, with 5V/3.1A total on the USB-C side. It carries 2400 joules of surge and overload protection, 1.7 inch spacing between outlets and a 0.5 inch 45 degree flat plug, on a 6 ft cord.

It leads because it solves the real desk problem: bulky adapters that block neighbors. The 1.7 inch spacing fits a laptop brick and a speaker adapter side by side. ALESTOR and Nuetsa offer 2700J, which is a higher joule figure, but they list fewer ports and neither names USB-C.

Buy it for a home office with a laptop, phone and tablet. The listing does not name a safety listing in our data, so check for ETL or UL marks before you buy, and note that 5V/3.1A is shared across the three USB-C ports.
products.idealFor: Home offices with chargers, laptops and bulky adapters.
products.skipIf: You need fast laptop charging over USB-C.

products.name: ALESTOR 12-Outlet Surge Protector with 4 USB Ports
products.verdict: 2700 joules, ETL listed and 12 outlets, the strongest surge spec with USB.
products.description:
ALESTOR's strip has 12 outlets, 4 USB ports, a 6 ft cord, 2700 joules of surge protection and an ETL listing, in the under $25 tier.

It earns second place because the joule rating and ETL mark are the most reassuring pairing of safety and capacity. Joules measure how much energy a surge protector can absorb before it fails, so 2700J outlasts the 1080J strips by a clear margin. It gives up only the USB-C ports that our top pick offers.

Buy it for a living room or workshop where many devices run at once. The USB side is basic and the listing names no USB-C, so a modern phone or tablet charges at ordinary speed.
products.idealFor: Entertainment centers and workshops with many plugs.
products.skipIf: You want USB-C for newer phones.

products.name: Nuetsa 8-Outlet Surge Protector with 4 USB Ports
products.verdict: 2700 joules, ETL listed and a flat plug, with four 5V/2.4A USB ports.
products.description:
The Nuetsa strip offers 8 outlets, 4 USB ports at 5V/2.4A, a 2700 joule rating, an ETL listing and a 6 ft cord with a flat plug.

It takes third because eight outlets suit most desks better than twelve, and the flat plug saves space behind furniture. Against the ALESTOR it matches the 2700J rating but has fewer outlets; against the 6-USB pick it has no USB-C.

Buy it for a bedroom or dorm where cord length and a slim plug matter. A 2.4A USB-A port charges a phone at roughly 12 watts, which suits phones but not laptops, so plan accordingly.
products.idealFor: Bedrooms and dorms needing a slim plug and USB.
products.skipIf: You need more than eight outlets.

products.name: Mifaso 10 ft Surge Protector with 4 USB Ports (2 USB-C)
products.verdict: A 10 ft braided cord, two USB-C ports and a fire-resistant shell.
products.description:
The Mifaso strip has 6 AC outlets rated 125V/15A/1875W, 2 USB-A ports at 5V/2.4A and 2 USB-C at 5V/3A, with 1080 joules, a 10 ft braided cord, a 45 degree flat plug and a fire-resistant shell rated to 1382°F. It is in the under $30 tier.

It sits fourth because the cord length is the selling point, and 10 ft reaches across a room from a distant outlet. Its 1080J rating is less than half of ALESTOR's, so it protects but does not rival the strongest surge spec.

Buy it for a desk far from the wall. A 5V/3A USB-C port is 15 watts, enough for phones but too low to fast-charge a laptop.
products.idealFor: Desks that sit far from a wall outlet.
products.skipIf: You want the highest surge rating.

products.name: HANYCONY 8-Outlet Surge Protector with 4 USB Ports (2 USB-C)
products.verdict: 8 outlets spaced 2.2 inches apart, with two USB-C ports and ETL certification.
products.description:
The HANYCONY strip has 8 widely spaced AC outlets, 4 USB ports including 2 USB-C at 5V/3A, 1080 joules of surge protection, a 5 ft braided cord and a flat plug. It is wall mountable, with RoHS and ETL certificates, in the under $30 tier.

It ranks fifth because the outlet spacing, 2.2 inches, is the widest here and takes oversized adapters. The surge rating is only 1080J and the cord is the shortest in the group.

Buy it for a desk full of power bricks. A 5 ft cord limits placement, so measure the distance from the wall first.
products.idealFor: Desks crowded with bulky power bricks.
products.skipIf: Your outlet is more than 5 ft away.

products.name: Yintar 6-Outlet Surge Protector with 3 USB Ports
products.verdict: A compact 6-outlet, 3-USB strip with 1680 joules and ETL listing.
products.description:
Yintar's strip has 6 AC outlets, 3 USB ports, 1680 joules, an ETL listing and a 6 ft cord in a compact design, in the under $25 tier.

It lands sixth because it is the smallest and simplest. Its 1680J beats the 1080J strips, but it trails ALESTOR and Nuetsa at 2700J, and the listing names no USB-C, so a modern phone charges at ordinary speed. It is a straightforward desk-corner strip with an ETL mark, which keeps it ahead of the Olcorife.

Buy it for a dorm or small desk. Six outlets fill fast once chunky adapters arrive, so count your plugs first.
products.skipIf: You need USB-C or many outlets.

products.name: Olcorife 10 ft Flat Plug Power Strip with 4 USB Ports
products.verdict: A 3-sided, wall-mountable strip with a 10 ft cord and a circuit breaker, but no joule rating.
products.description:
The Olcorife strip has 8 widely spaced outlets, 3 USB-A ports and 1 USB-C, a 3-sided design, a 10 ft cord, a 0.27 inch ultra-thin flat plug, two wall-mount holes and a built-in circuit breaker. It is in the under $30 bracket.

It ranks last because the listing describes overload protection but no joule rating, so it is not clearly a surge protector. A circuit breaker stops overcurrent; it does not absorb voltage spikes.

Buy it for a travel or dorm setup where size and cord length matter. For a desk with expensive electronics, choose one of the joule-rated strips above.
products.idealFor: Dorms and travel where size and cord length matter.

whatMatters.detail: Joules measure how much surge energy a protector can soak up before its protective components wear out. Here 1080J is basic, Yintar's 1680J is mid, the top pick's 2400J is strong and ALESTOR and Nuetsa reach 2700J. Higher lasts longer under repeated spikes. Look for a stated joule figure, and treat a listing without one with suspicion.

ETL and UL marks show a lab checked the strip against a safety standard, which matters more than any marketing number because it covers fire risk. ALESTOR, Nuetsa, Mifaso, HANYCONY and Yintar list ETL, while the 12-outlet leader names none in our data. Look for the mark in the listing text or photos, and ignore the bare word certified.

USB-C wattage decides whether a port is useful beyond a phone. A 5V/2.4A USB-A port gives roughly 12 watts, and a 5V/3A USB-C port gives 15, both far below a laptop charger. The 12-outlet leader shares 5V/3.1A across three USB-C ports. Check output per port on the listing, and plug laptops into an AC outlet.

Outlet spacing determines whether you can use every socket. Chunky adapters block neighbors on a tight strip. The 12-outlet leader spaces them 1.7 inches apart and HANYCONY 2.2, enough for two bricks side by side, while Olcorife also advertises wide spacing. Check the stated inches or look at the listing photos before you count outlets.

A circuit breaker and a surge protector do different jobs. A breaker trips when current runs too high, protecting the wiring, while surge protection absorbs voltage spikes measured in joules. The Olcorife lists a breaker and no joule rating, so it guards against overload only. Check that the listing names a joule figure, not just overload protection.

faq.a: Not quickly. The Mifaso and HANYCONY list USB-C at 5V/3A, which is 15 watts, well below a laptop charger's output. Plug the laptop's own charger into an AC outlet on the 12-outlet pick or ALESTOR, and use USB for phones.

Trusting a circuit breaker as surge protection. The Olcorife lists a breaker and no joule rating, so it stops an overload but will not absorb a voltage spike. If the listing names no joules, treat it as an extension cord.

faq.q: Is a surge protector worth it over a plain strip?
faq.a: Yes for anything with a circuit board. ALESTOR's 2700 joules costs under $25 and can absorb a spike that would damage a computer, while a plain strip passes the spike straight through. Replace the strip once its protection light goes out.

faq.q: How do I set it up?
faq.a: Plug it into a wall outlet, never another strip, and check the protection light. A flat plug like the Nuetsa's or the 12-outlet pick's 0.5 inch plug fits behind furniture. Arrange big adapters first, then fill the gaps with slim plugs.

Surge protectors wear out with every spike, so replace one every few years or after a major storm. Check that the indicator light is on, and treat a dark light as a retired strip, even if the outlets still deliver power.

faq.q: Can I run a space heater on it?
faq.a: No. A space heater draws close to the 1875W limit the Mifaso lists, and strips overheat under that load. Plug heaters, toasters and similar loads directly into the wall, and keep the strip for electronics.

finalTake: The 12-outlet strip with six USB ports and 2400 joules is the one to buy for a modern desk, and ALESTOR is the safest if you want the highest surge rating. Mifaso reaches farthest and Nuetsa fits behind furniture. Check certification marks, and keep heaters off every strip.
